dedupe_keys.name: nist investigation of the champlain towers south partial collapse surfside florida

description: On 24 June 2021 Champlain Towers South, a 12-floor condominium in Surfside, Florida, partially collapsed at about 1:30 a.m., causing mass casualties. NIST began deploying a team of six scientists and engineers the next day and, as a National Construction Safety Team investigation, worked with federal, state and local authorities to identify and preserve materials and information, inviting the public to submit video, photographs and documents through the NIST Disaster Data Portal. Its technical findings, released on 22 June 2026, trace the start of the collapse to failed connections between garage columns and the pool deck, with the failure spreading into the tower; an annual report to Congress summarises progress, and an advisory committee meeting was set for 23 and 24 September 2026. Coverage: one building in Surfside, Florida. Access: the NIST investigation page with news, reports and video. Licence: U.S. government work; free. Caveats: the final report and recommendations may follow the technical findings, so later documents should be checked. Simulation uses are as a benchmark for progressive collapse of reinforced concrete buildings and for condition assessment of ageing structures. Related records: the NIST World Trade Center investigation.

name: NIST investigation of the Champlain Towers South partial collapse (Surfside, Florida)
outcomes: NIST released technical findings on 22 June 2026: after examining two dozen scenarios, the team concluded that the collapse began in early June 2021 when two connections between garage columns and the pool deck failed, shifting load to elements too weak to carry it because of problems stemming from original design and construction, and the pool deck slab breaking away then damaged connections supporting the tower.
provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), National Construction Safety Team
resources_used: Materials and information preserved at the collapse site
Public submissions through the NIST Disaster Data Portal
Structural analysis of two dozen collapse initiation scenarios
